answer: Broca's area is a region in the dominant hemisphere's frontal lobe, typically the left, that functions in speech production [Web: Broca's area (Wikipedia)]. It is located in the posterior inferior frontal gyrus (pars triangularis) [Web: Broca's area (Wikipedia)]. This region is also associated with speech formation and is part of the prefrontal cortex [Web: Prefrontal cortex (Wikipedia)]. Ask for more detail if you need it.

The thyroglossal duct is a structure typically present only during embryonic growth [Web: Persistent thyroglossal duct (Wikipedia)]. It forms a midline connection between the thyroid gland and the back of the tongue [Web: Persistent thyroglossal duct (Wikipedia)]. This duct runs anterior to the sternohyoid muscle, sternothyroid muscle, and thyrohyoid membrane [Web: Persistent thyroglossal duct (Wikipedia)]. It also stays close to the neck's medial line and anterior to the laryngeal cartilage [Web: Persistent thyroglossal duct (Wikipedia)].

The glomus tympanicum is an ovoid body of highly vascular chemoreceptive tissue located next to the tympanic cavity [Web: MeSH: Glomus Tympanicum (NLM MeSH)]. It originates from neural crest tissue and is part of the diffuse neuroendocrine system [Web: MeSH: Glomus Tympanicum (NLM MeSH)]. This area is the location for a rare neoplasm known as a glomus tympanicum tumor [Web: MeSH: Glomus Tympanicum Tumor (NLM MeSH)].

Waldeyer's tonsillar ring is a collection of lymphoid organs that face into the aerodigestive tract [Web: Tonsil (Wikipedia)]. This ring includes the lingual tonsils, two palatine tonsils, two tubal tonsils, and the pharyngeal (adenoid) tonsil [Web: Tonsil (Wikipedia)]. These organs serve a significant role within the immune system [Web: Tonsil (Wikipedia)].

answer: Calot's triangle, also called the cystohepatic or hepatobiliary triangle, is an anatomic space [Web: Cystohepatic triangle (Wikipedia)]. It is bordered by the common hepatic duct medially, the cystic duct laterally, and the liver's inferior surface superiorly [Web: Cystohepatic triangle (Wikipedia)]. The cystic artery and cystic node are located within this triangle [Web: Cystohepatic triangle (Wikipedia)] [Web: Cystic node (Wikipedia)]. Ask for more detail if you need it.

q: What is the sphincter of Oddi?
answer:
The sphincter of Oddi is a circular muscle band that surrounds the major duodenal papilla [Web: Sphincter of Oddi (Wikipedia)]. This muscular valve regulates the flow of pancreatic juice and bile through the ampulla of Vater into the duodenum [Web: Sphincter of Oddi (Wikipedia)]. The main pancreatic duct and common bile duct travel through this sphincter [Web: MeSH: Sphincter of Oddi (NLM MeSH)]. It is also known as Glisson's sphincter or the hepatopancreatic sphincter [Web: Sphincter of Oddi (Wikipedia)].
